sub_questions.question: Why does it say I'm out of credits when I haven't used the app much?
Can you fix this (restore the ability to use the app)?

claims.claim: The credit allowance differs depending on the workspace's plan.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew) ... Professional ... 5,000 credits/month ... Team ... 10,000 credits/month

claims.claim: On the free Sandbox plan, the 200 message credits are a one-time allowance that doesn't renew.
Even light use can exhaust the Sandbox allowance.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models ... around 10 credits per response. A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: On Professional or Team, credits reset monthly.
claims.guide_evidence: waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans) — Sandbox credits do not reset

claims.claim: Some responses cost more credits than others; a heavier model can burn through the balance faster than expected.
claims.guide_evidence: Message credits are not consumed at a flat rate. Each model response is metered in credits according to the specific model used

claims.claim: The Billing page shows the workspace's plan and remaining credits.
claims.guide_evidence: Only the workspace owner and admins can open the Billing page and manage a subscription.

claims.claim: Options include connecting your own provider key or upgrading.
claims.guide_evidence: model calls on Dify-hosted credits stop working until the workspace either connects its own API key for that provider or waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans)

evaluation.rationale: The answer correctly explains, using the guide, both likely causes: Sandbox's one-time 200 credits and per-model credit metering on paid plans. Asking which plan Dana is on is reasonable because the fix depends on the plan, and the options it names (connect a provider key or upgrade) are grounded in the guide. It doesn't mention that only owners and admins can open the Billing page, but that is a small omission and causes no harm.
